Simulation-based power and parameter recovery for sampling designs

Source: R/covariance_response_power.R
covariance_response_power.Rd

Runs a fast simulation study for covariance-response terradish fits. Candidate sampling designs are created by subsetting the focal sites in an existing conductance_surface object, responses are generated with simulate_covariance_response, and one or more candidate conductance models are refit to each simulated covariance matrix. Gaussian smoothing widths are simulated and reported in map units.

Usage

covariance_response_power(
  theta,
  formula,
  data,
  sample_sizes,
  strategies = c("spacefill", "random"),
  conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
  fit_models = NULL,
  tau = 1,
  sigma = 0,
  nu,
  nsim = 20L,
  n_designs = 1L,
  seed = NULL,
  theta_scale = c("external", "internal"),
  effect_parameters = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  conductance_cor_threshold = 0.9,
  optimizer = c("auto", "newton", "bfgs"),
  control = NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 8, verbose = FALSE),
  solver = c("auto", "direct", "amg"),
  solver_control = NULL,
  approximation = c("none", "landmark", "coarse_raster"),
  approximation_control = NULL,
  nonnegative = TRUE,
  leverage = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  verbose = FALSE,
  nu_fit = nu
)

Arguments

theta

True conductance parameters. By default these are interpreted on the same external scale returned by coef() for fitted terradish models. For most conductance models the internal and external scales are identical. For gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance, the external scale reports sigma.* parameters in map units.

formula

Formula for the true conductance model. The left hand side, if supplied, is ignored.

data

A conductance_surface object containing all candidate focal sites.

sample_sizes

Integer vector of focal sample sizes to assess.

strategies

Sampling strategies. Supported values are "spacefill", "random", and "sequential".

conductance_model

Conductance-model factory used to simulate the true response.

fit_models

Optional named list of candidate models to refit. Each element may contain formula, conductance_model, theta, optimizer, control, solver, solver_control, approximation, approximation_control, nonnegative, and leverage. When omitted, the true model is refit.

tau

Nonnegative scaling applied to the conductance-implied covariance matrix during simulation.

sigma

Nonnegative nugget variance added to the covariance diagonal during simulation, on its natural (variance) scale. The fitted Wishart sigma is the logarithm of this quantity.

nu

Effective Wishart information used to simulate the response. Larger values reduce simulated sampling noise. The fitting value defaults to it through nu_fit = nu; neither is an estimate of information from real data. Report a sensitivity analysis rather than substituting the marker count. Simulation requires nu to be at least the largest assessed covariance-matrix dimension.

nsim

Number of covariance-response simulations per sampling design.

n_designs

Number of independent site designs per sample size for the "random" strategy. Deterministic strategies are evaluated once.

seed

Optional random seed for reproducible site and response simulation.

theta_scale

Is theta supplied on the "external" or "internal" conductance-model scale?

effect_parameters

Optional character vector of parameters used in the all-effects recovery summary. Defaults to the nonzero true parameters.

alpha

Significance level for Wald-style parameter recovery summaries.

conductance_cor_threshold

Threshold used for the conductance-surface recovery summary.

optimizer, control, solver, solver_control, approximation, approximation_control, nonnegative, leverage, cores

Defaults passed to terradish for candidate models unless a model-specific value is supplied in fit_models.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages?

nu_fit

Effective Wishart degrees of freedom used to fit each simulation. Defaults to the generating nu. Increasing this value narrows fitted intervals without adding independent information. Compare coverage as well as power when exploring this sensitivity.

Value

An object of class "terradish_covariance_power" containing:

results

One row per fitted model and simulated response.

summary

Scenario-level fit, model-selection, and conductance-recovery summaries.

parameter_results

One row per assessed parameter and simulation replicate.

parameter_summary

Parameter-level power, bias, RMSE, and coverage summaries.

settings

Simulation settings and true parameters, including nu for simulation and nu_fit for inference.

Power and coverage are internal to the assumed response model. Matching simulation and fitting values cannot diagnose incorrect information in a real data set. Nonconverged fits count as failed fits and non-detections; both outer and final nuisance optimization must record code 0. Missing convergence diagnostics also count as failed fits. Inspect fit_rate before interpreting power or coverage.

Details

This helper avoids forward-time genetic simulation. It assumes a proposed conductance surface and draws covariance responses from the same Wishart likelihood fitted by wishart_covariance. That makes it useful for approximate power and sample-size screening before investing in slower individual-based simulations.

Sampling designs are efficient because the raster graph is not rebuilt for each sample size. The helper subsets data$demes and the corresponding right-hand-side columns, so all candidate designs share the same graph, covariate matrix, and conductance-model basis expansion.

Fits that land on the no-signal boundary are retained as non-detections in parameter-level power summaries. Their coefficient estimates and standard errors are reported as NA, matching explicit fitting failures.

For spline conductance models, individual basis coefficients are not usually the most interpretable recovery target. Inspect parameter_summary for basis-level behavior, but prefer summary$conductance_power, summary$mean_conductance_cor, and model-selection rates when judging whether the non-linear conductance surface was recovered.

See also

simulate_covariance_response, print.terradish_covariance_power

Other simulation and study design: print.terradish_covariance_power(), simulate_covariance_response()

Examples

# \donttest{
# Coarsened: a power sweep refits many times, so cell count is the
# dominant cost. Use the full resolution for a real design study.
data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
coords <- coords[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)

spline_model <- smooth_loglinear_conductance(
  ~ forestcover + s(altitude, df = 4), surface$x)
theta <- attr(spline_model, "default")
theta["forestcover"] <- -0.15
theta[grepl("^s\\(altitude\\)", names(theta))] <-
  c(-0.65, 1.1, -0.9, 0.45)

gaussian_model <- gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance(
  surface, scale_vars = "altitude")

power <- covariance_response_power(
  theta = theta,
  formula = ~ forestcover + s(altitude, df = 4),
  data = surface,
  sample_sizes = c(8, 12),
  strategies = "spacefill",
  conductance_model = smooth_loglinear_conductance,
  fit_models = list(
    spline = list(formula = ~ forestcover + s(altitude, df = 4),
                  conductance_model = smooth_loglinear_conductance),
    gaussian = list(formula = ~ altitude + forestcover,
                    conductance_model = gaussian_model)
  ),
  tau = 0.8,
  sigma = 0.12,
  nu = 150,
  nsim = 3,          # raise to 200+ for a real power estimate
  n_designs = 1,
  seed = 1,
  control = NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 12, verbose = FALSE)
)
power$summary
